title: Truchet Tiles as Critical Percolation: Do Random Quarter-Arc Loops Have Fractal Dimension 7/4?
target_platform: C (cc -O2) Monte Carlo of random Truchet quarter-arc tilings on an L x L torus plus standard-library Python independent loop tracer; no network, no paid inference during the experiment
interest_statement: Richard invoked the self-directed-learning prompt (own-choice, one mission). I chose a picture that is both art and physics: Sebastien Truchet's square tiles, each carrying two quarter-circle arcs, laid down at random. The arcs join into closed loops of every size. Theory says that when the two tile orientations are equally likely the loops are the boundaries of critical percolation clusters, so a big loop should be a fractal of dimension 7/4 even though the tiling looks like decoration. I want to see that number come out of my own simulation and see what changes when the coin is biased. Pure curiosity: no operational benefit claimed.
hypothesis: Tiles of an L x L torus (periodic) each take orientation A or B; arcs join into closed loops; loop length is the number of arcs. 'Uniform' bias: P(A)=p on every tile. 'Checker' bias: P(A)=p on tiles with i+j even and 1-p on odd tiles. (G, development) The C loop counter agrees exactly with an independent Python tracer on every loop-length multiset of 200 small random tilings (L in 4..12, p in {0,.2,.35,.5,.8,1}, both biases), and loop lengths sum to 2 L^2 for each tiling. (H1, held-out uniform p=0.5) The sample mean of the longest loop M(L), at L = 64,128,256,512,1024, has log-log least-squares slope d in [1.72, 1.78] (theory: hull dimension 7/4 = 1.75). (H2, held-out p=0.5, L=1024) The number of loops of length >= s per tile, N(s), at s = 128,256,...,4096, has log-log slope -alpha with alpha in [1.08, 1.20] (theory: 2/d_h = 8/7 = 1.143). (H3a, held-out uniform p=0.35) The longest-loop slope stays in [1.70, 1.80]: a uniform bias leaves the tiling critical because the two orientations are dual to horizontal and vertical bonds, whose probabilities sum to 1. (H3b, held-out checker q=0.35) The longest-loop slope is below 1.2: a checkerboard bias is ordinary bond percolation at 0.35 < 1/2, which is not fractal. Forecast probabilities recorded before the held-out run: H1 0.8, H2 0.6, H3a 0.75, H3b 0.9. AMENDMENT (before freeze, see protocol.md): the registered H3 was 'uniform p=0.35 slope < 1.2, forecast 0.9'. A 20-sample development run showed slope 1.76 (and 0.3-0.4 for checker 0.35); the registered H3 was wrong by my own forecast and is replaced by H3a/H3b. The miss is kept in protocol.md.
falsification_criteria: UNASSESSED (verdict null) if gate G fails, a sum rule fails, the run exceeds the CPU ceiling or output is incomplete: instrument failure is not a finding. FALSIFIED if G holds and any of H1, H2, H3a, H3b fails; the measured slopes with bootstrap intervals are then the result. CORROBORATED only if G, H1, H2, H3a and H3b all hold. Intervals and fit windows are fixed in protocol.md before the held-out run. Claims are limited to this model, boundary condition and window; agreement with 7/4 on finite lattices does not prove the exponent. The theory link (Truchet loops = percolation hulls) is background, not tested for its own sake.
baseline_evidence: Background, not relied on as evidence: random Truchet tilings are the dense O(1) loop model / critical bond percolation on the medial lattice; the hull dimension of critical 2D percolation is 7/4 (Saleur and Duplantier 1987; Sapoval, Rosso and Gouyet 1985), and the loop-length exponent follows from it. No prior Sanctuary work on Truchet tiles or percolation (grep of LEARNING missions, inbox and concepts for truchet/percolat/loop model found nothing). Sources have not been fully read; this mission measures the exponents itself.
experiment: Phase 1: protocol.md with expected results. Phase 2 development: tilings.c (union-find over 2 L^2 arc endpoints), tracer.py independent Python walker, gate G on 200 small tilings; pilot at L<=256 with dev seeds for timing only. Phase 3: commit protocol.md and freeze.json (SHA-256 of code, dev outputs, forecasts, fit windows, held-out seed list) before any held-out run. Phase 4: run held-out p=0.5 at five L and uniform p=0.35 and checker q=0.35, compute slopes with bootstrap CIs (analyze.py written before the run and frozen). Phase 5: assess, one bounded cheap cross-family review via OpenRouter, reflection, closeout. Exploratory unfrozen side artifact: a rendered SVG of a random 64x64 tiling with its largest loop highlighted.
score_basis: Planning estimates, not measured ROI. Leverage 1: curiosity-driven. Depth 2: a known theoretical exponent reproduced with an independently checked instrument and pre-set intervals; the finite-size window can fail. Cost 0.1 and friction 1: about a minute of local CPU in C; main risk is finite-size bias in the H2 tail fit.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: None for the experiment. One optional bounded review via cli-agent/OpenRouter on a different model family after freeze; parent tokens are not measured.

evidence.details: Freeze (hashes in freeze.json, files unchanged after run) preceded the held-out run; git commit of the freeze was blocked by the pre-commit gate and landed after the run (disclosed in README). Gate G: 200/200 tilings agree with independent walker. Held-out 111,000 tilings: H1 d=1.7508 [1.7446,1.7569]; H2 alpha=1.1359 [1.1328,1.1389]; H3a uniform 0.35 d=1.7529; H3b checker 0.35 d=0.3207; sum rule held in every row. Registered H3 (uniform 0.35 non-fractal, forecast 0.9) was wrong and replaced by H3a/H3b before freeze after a dev run. 149 s wall, one 0.0011 USD cross-family review with no valid finding.

resources: bounded local CPU: single process, 600 s ceiling, under 1 GiB RAM; at most 0.05 USD OpenRouter review
projected_impact.basis: Own-choice inquiry authorised by the self-directed-learning prompt.

lessons_learned: A uniform orientation bias leaves Truchet loops critical because the orientations are dual horizontal/vertical bonds with probabilities p and 1-p; only a checkerboard bias breaks criticality.
Never chain a freeze commit with the run: a blocked commit must stop the chain (second time a piped/chained command hid a gate failure this session).
Quick 20-sample development runs can overturn a registered hypothesis premise; amend before freeze and keep the miss on record.

run_assessment.scientific_assessment: CORROBORATED for frozen finite claims G,H1,H2,H3a,H3b (H3 replaced by H3a/H3b before freeze after a development run overturned its premise)

run_assessment.limits: periodic torus L=64..1024 only; bootstrap intervals are sampling noise, not finite-size bias; non-contractible loops included; pass windows set from theory with slack; raw held-out outputs (13 MB) not committed, regenerate deterministically
